implemented_requirements.requirement: Two vertical paddles controllable by separate keys (up/down) for each player
implemented_requirements.evidence: paddle.py defines a Paddle class with `up_key` and `down_key` arguments, updates position based on `pygame.key.get_pressed()`, and clamps movement within the screen.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball moves and bounces off the top and bottom edges of the playfield
implemented_requirements.evidence: ball.py implements `_bounce_off_walls()` which inverts the vertical velocity when `self.y` reaches 0 or `SCREEN_HEIGHT - size`.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces off paddles with angle variation and speed increase
implemented_requirements.evidence: ball.py defines `bounce_off_paddle()` that calculates an offset‑based angle, multiplies speed by `BALL_SPEEDUP`, and reverses horizontal direction. game.py calls this method in `handle_paddle_collisions()`.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py `handle_scoring()` checks `ball.rect.right < 0` and `ball.rect.left > SCREEN_WIDTH` and calls `award_point()` which updates the Scoreboard.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Winning score threshold ends the match
implemented_requirements.evidence: scoreboard.py stores `WINNING_SCORE` and `get_winner()` returns a player index when a score reaches that value. game.py switches to `STATE_GAME_OVER` when a winner is found.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball is reset and served after each point
implemented_requirements.evidence: ball.reset() exists, but `award_point()` contains an ellipsis (`...`) instead of calling `ball.reset()`. Also `restart_match()` calls `ball.reset(direction=-1, immediate=False)` which does not match the `reset` signature (only `direction`). The serve timer is never initialized on the first serve.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game loop with rendering of paddles, ball, and scoreboard
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py defines `run()`, `handle_events()`, `update()`, but the `draw()` method is not present in the provided snippet. `scoreboard.draw()` also contains an ellipsis, so no rendering code is available.

critical_issues: `award_point()` in game.py ends with an ellipsis (`...`) – the logic that resets the ball and sets the serve direction is missing, causing a syntax error and preventing point‑reset behavior.
`restart_match()` calls `ball.reset(direction=-1, immediate=False)`, but `Ball.reset()` only accepts a single `direction` argument; the extra `immediate` argument will raise a TypeError.
`draw()` method for Game and `draw()` method for Scoreboard are not implemented (contain `...`), so the program cannot render any graphics.
The initial `serve_timer` is set to 0.0 and never initialized to `SERVE_DELAY` before the first serve, meaning the ball will never launch.
Missing import or reference errors may arise because the incomplete code sections are syntactically invalid.
judge.summary: The repository contains substantial core logic for a two‑player Pong game: paddle movement, ball physics, wall and paddle collisions, scoring, and win detection are all present. However, several essential pieces are incomplete or incorrect—most notably the point‑reset flow, mismatched method signatures, and missing rendering code. These gaps make the program non‑executable in its current state and prevent it from fully satisfying the benchmark requirements.
